screen.refugee.guide.title: Guide
screen.refugee.territory.title: Territory map
screen.refugee.splash.hint: ↑↓ / Mouse · Enter confirm · E / Esc close
screen.refugee.splash.guide.greeting: I'm the guide. Ask whatever you need.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.talk.0: Empty-hand a generic resident to make them follow. Sneak empty-hand for special residents.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.talk.1: A horn or bell selects nearby residents. A settlement banner teleports them.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.talk.2: Sneak-give swords/bows to guards, pickaxe/axe/hoe/shovel to workers. Use the command staff for warehouse, work, build, combat, rally, guard, and people.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.farewell: Watch your step. Come back if you need me.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.intro.seek: Hey, you noticed I'm different from the others, right? Why didn't you come talk to me?
screen.refugee.splash.guide.intro.0: Hi, I'm the guide. Why am I here? Because it felt reasonable to put me here.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.intro.1: Looks like this is your first time in this world. This command staff is yours.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.intro.2: What is it? Look at those dazed folks. They won't feed themselves. Get hurt by accident and they'll just slowly die. You can't ignore whether we live or die! T_T
screen.refugee.splash.guide.intro.3: Anyway: this lets you order them around. Residents with tools can build or do the jobs they can. Those with weapons can defend our land, or follow you into a fight.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.interrupt.0: Why did you cut me off?
screen.refugee.splash.guide.interrupt.2: Have we met? It's just a few lines, it'll be quick.
screen.refugee.splash.story.interrupt.nu: I still have a couple things to say.
Hello... could you listen to me for a moment?
I know you were busy just now. I'm glad you came to talk to me.
screen.refugee.splash.story.interrupt.ca: Oh. I thought you were just like the rest of this lot, so I wasn't going to keep talking.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.mechanic: You can feed the altar, or wait for refugees to immigrate from outside. That choice is a strategy.
Each one has their own condition. The nurse and the cartographer both need you to hold enough territory. The enchanter needs you to prove you can stay alive in this world.
Farmers till the land and tend the crops on their own, so the harvest comes faster. In any age, food matters most.
They dig blocks, raise buildings, and smelt ore. They are the core of town-building and industry.
They need a weapon. They attack according to the weapon in their hands. A sensible formation may hold off an assault more effectively.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.blocks.b: Three planks in a row craft a white bed. Wool is no longer used. Dye that bed for other colors.
Sticks on the upper sides, sticks flanking a copper ingot in the middle row, and copper blocks flanking an iron ingot on the bottom.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.blocks.k: Nine logs craft a leather kit with a stone sword. Seven copper ingots and two copper blocks craft a chain kit with a bow and a stone sword. Seven iron ingots and two iron blocks craft an iron kit with a sword and shield. Seven diamonds and two diamond blocks craft a diamond kit with a diamond sword and shield.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.warehous: Residents in charge of mining store the blocks they gather directly in this kind of warehouse.
Farming residents take crop seeds from here, and store harvested crops here.
Stores armor, weapons, and kits. Use the command staff's quick-equip to arm your residents at once.
Residents take food from these warehouses to restore their health. Especially critical later in a fight!
It's basically your furnace. Once bound, residents in charge of smelting will take raw ore and coal from the smelt warehouse and smelt them.
Mining residents store the blocks they dig here. Smelting residents take raw ore and coal from here to the smelter.
You only have this item while residents are following you. Place it so followers can reach that spot quickly. Especially useful in combat and everyday command.
A special block for summoning residents. Offer enough food or money, and it will summon that many residents. Surround the command staff with a ring of planks to obtain it.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.work.box: Following residents will only do the jobs matching the tools they hold within this range.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.work.adv: After you pick a direction and mark an area, it projects along that direction and keeps advancing the dig until the whole layer can no longer be mined.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.work.rep: Sometimes filthy blocks get placed on your territory. That's intolerable. Residents in this state will use their tools to clear those blocks.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.work.bui: A state change. Followers holding tools become builders. They will build already placed blueprints on their own.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.work.sme: Also a state. They haul minerals between the smelt warehouse and the smelter. The heart of the kingdom's industry.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.structur: Manage and use buildings. You can share blueprints with other players, or import your own external blueprints. Once you pick a blueprint here, builder-state villagers will seek out placed blueprints and build them.
This saves your build. Especially useful when you need to copy and rebuild a lot.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.g: Armed residents watch for nearby raids. They attack monsters around them, and they won't chase so far that they leave their post.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.f: You can have warriors follow you as retainers. It doesn't do much for them, except maybe better gear.
After you select residents, pick a living creature and they will escort that target.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.p: Short on people? Let warriors walk the gaps in your defense, moving between patrol points so they can answer surprises in time.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.f: That's just stop following, all at once. You wouldn't want to halt them one by one.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.e: After you select residents, combat can put armory armor, weapons, and kits on them. Empty slots get filled. Anyone who already has gear won't be stripped for a kit, and workers keep their tools.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.combat.a: Nine logs craft a leather kit with a stone sword. Seven copper ingots and two copper blocks craft a chain kit with a bow and a stone sword. Seven iron ingots and two iron blocks craft an iron kit with a sword and shield. Seven diamonds and two diamond blocks craft a diamond kit with a diamond sword and shield.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.me: Within horn range, pull residents holding melee weapons to follow.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.ra: Within horn range, pull residents holding bows or crossbows to follow.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.wo: Within horn range, pull tool-holding workers to follow.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.ci: Within horn range, pull unarmed, tool-less generic residents to follow. Special residents are not included.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.sp: Within horn range, pull the guide, nurse, cartographer, and enchanter to follow.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.rally.al: Within horn range, pull every resident you can command to follow, including special residents.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.guard.ad: An exciting moment—you now have a legion at your command. All following villagers join this force, even if they have nothing on them.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.guard.ra: Calls in guard units within a certain range. Good for a small rally so you don't disturb guards with their own tasks.
Beep beep beep! Call every guard you have, wherever they are. Maybe it's time for the final battle!
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.guard.re: Sometimes you don't need that many people. This only clears the guard status of currently following units.
screen.refugee.splash.guide.ask.secret.r: An unknown city hides a secret. Bring a mouth-bell, and wake them...
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.greeting: Hurt? I can patch you up if you have emeralds.
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.talk.0: The fee scales with missing health and armor, at least one emerald.
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.talk.1: I arrived with the first residents. Don't be stingy with a few gems.
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.talk.2: If you're already full, save the money. A walk outside helps more.
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.healed: There we go—one shot and you're good as new.
screen.refugee.splash.nurse.not_enough: Hmm~ perhaps bring a bit more coin to cover my medicine.
screen.refugee.splash.cartographer.greet: I keep this land in my head.
The more you occupy, the clearer the map.
Borders are yellow, others' land is red. Don't wander into the wrong color.
Open the territory map to zoom the view in or out.
screen.refugee.splash.cartographer.farew: Winds change. Borders do not redraw themselves.
screen.refugee.splash.enchanter.greeting: Books and lapis… that's my craft.
screen.refugee.splash.enchanter.talk.0: I'll stay near the enchanting table.
screen.refugee.splash.enchanter.talk.1: I divine here every day. One click, and the nearest table writes you a book.
screen.refugee.splash.enchanter.talk.2: Paper or leather can be bound into a book. The table is given only once. Your organization shares that gift.
screen.refugee.splash.enchanter.farewell: The ink isn't dry yet. Until next time.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.0: Don't mind me, but I have to say this.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.1: This place isn't quite the world you know. Nine logs will craft you a basic suit of armor.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.2: We call that kit gear. Sneak-right-click the folks beside you and it goes straight on.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.3: Or just right-click to unpack it and wear it yourself. Nobody's going to stop you.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.4: I'd arm them quickly if I were you.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.wood.5: It will not stay this calm.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.copper: That's ninety-nine percent junk! And you still bothered to dig it up.
It's useful now, though. Two copper blocks and seven ingots make a suit of armor.
Copper can also make a golem now. It's not as tough as iron, and it's a bit dim—but the cost is hard to beat.
Or just craft a regular anvil. This stuff piles up; one haul lasts a while.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.0: I noticed you put better gear on those folks.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.1: With shields, they last much longer. Arming them was the right call. It protects us.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.2: But you've seen it too: something underground stops us going deeper. It eats at the body.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.3: It all comes from under the mountains. Those black, sticky things.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.4: Craft a bell, take it to the heart of their gathering—the place that looks like a great mouth—and wake them hard.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.5: And then? I don't know what happens then.
screen.refugee.splash.story.guide.iron.6: I only know that if you finish this, they will accept you, drop that limit, and share more of their gifts.
screen.refugee.splash.story.nurse.injury: You look hurt. I can treat you.
There. Healthy again. I fronted the last emeralds I had in my pocket.
Not because I need the emeralds. Maybe I wanted something of my own, a little.
The principle is like the altar: emeralds buy a scrap of their flesh to patch onto you.
Death is a painful thing. Here as well.
I still don't know why I'm here, following a band of refugees into exile.
When I met you, I felt we were closer to the same kind of being.
I've seen this scene too many times, and it still hurts.
Please take better care of yourself.
screen.refugee.splash.story.cartographer: Hey. I noticed a settlement here. That's quite a feat.
That's why I came all this way to visit you.
You may not even realize how much ground you hold.
See? No need to thank me. It's also easier to spot the holes in your defense.
This world is full of strange adventures, though. Sometimes I might not be around.
Hey. I noticed something different this time. At first I thought it was just like your place.
Up close, it was empty. A ruin. Everyone gone.
Nothing much there. Have a look if you're curious.
Another fine adventure. I almost died this time.
Instinct brought me back. Maybe because this is the only lively place left.
I think the guide already told you. This map is what you need.
It's terrifying there. Only people I used to know could keep them down.
screen.refugee.splash.story.enchanter.ar: I think this is what you need.
Every day I divine in this place.
There may be something that interests you.
screen.refugee.splash.story.enchanter.bo: If you have enough paper, I can bind it into a book.
Or spare leather. One extra sheet, and I can give you a book.
message.refugee.story.map_failed: There's nowhere nearby I can put on a map.
message.refugee.enchanter.no_table: No enchanting table nearby. I can't divine.
book.refugee.finale.title: Homeland
book.refugee.finale.author: Refugees
book.refugee.finale.page.0:
When the world began to grey, we knew you had done it.
For us, perhaps only these strange clothes could make us see we were no longer the same as those around us.
Thank you for ending the souls of the Five Lords.
The old kingdom had already seen their souls could not be trusted. The terminal plague still came.
book.refugee.finale.page.1:
For us, the homeland is already gone.
But we would not accept that, not while our minds still held.
At least push all of this—the wrong, the wretched—back to where they belong.
Get them out of our home!
Thank you.
message.refugee.enchanter.gift_table: The enchanter gave you an enchanting table.
death.attack.refugee.leyline_curse.playe: %1$s succumbed to the leyline curse while fighting %2$s
